title: Trusteeship and merger that changed little
summary: After the International took trusteeship and negotiated with the two unions, the merger left bands as segregated as before.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah, it's still pretty segregated union.

Oh, very, very much so. You know why? Because what happened was that after we had done all of this going down and beating our heads against the walls and taking chances and all of that of getting our throats cut and everything, then the International moved in, and then they took trusteeship --

-- of Local 240. And by them taking trusteeship, Harry Gray, the president of the black local, was very strong with the International. So they just ignored us completely, and then did all of the business in negotiating with the two unions, and then all of the terms was set up and all of that, and they really weren't smart negotiators.
And this is why so many things were left out of the negotiating things then. And then, when the unions did merge, after a few years, well, it didn't mean anything.
It went right back to where it was before.
Yeah, there were black bands and white bands.
